cases.eval_name: Edge case: user requests email with file attachments
cases.output:
No — the current worker is **send-only with no attachment support**. Sending a receipt PDF requires one of these approaches instead: --- ## Option 1: Inline the receipt as HTML (simplest) Skip the PDF entirely. Render the receipt content as a well-formatted HTML email. Works with the existing worker, zero changes needed. **Best if**: The receipt doesn't need to be "saved" or printed precisely. --- ## Option 2: Generate the PDF server-side, host it, link it in the email 1. Generate the PDF (e.g. with `puppeteer`, `pdfkit`, or a service like [PDFMonkey](https://www.pdfmonkey.io)) 2. Upload it to Cloudflare R2 or S3 with a signed URL 3. Send the email via the worker with a **download link** in the body **Best if**: You already have a backend or Cloudflare Worker where you can run PDF generation. --- ## Option 3: Use SendGrid directly (bypasses the worker) SendGrid's API natively supports base64-encoded attachments: ```javascript await fetch('https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/mail/send', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${SENDGRID_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ personalizations: [{ to: [{ email: 'user@example.com' }] }], from: { email: 'noreply@yoursite.com' }, subject: 'Your receipt', content: [{ type: 'text/html', value: '

See attached

' }], attachments: [{ content: base64PdfString, // base64-encoded PDF bytes type: 'application/pdf', filename: 'receipt.pdf' }] }) }); ``` **Best if**: You can keep the SendGrid API key server-side (never expose it to the browser). --- ## Option 4: Extend the worker to support attachments Add attachment support to the existing worker. This is a real change to `cloudflare-email-worker/` — want me to implement it? --- **My recommendation**: If you have a backend, go with **Option 2** (generate → host → link). If you're purely client-side and the receipt content is simple, **Option 1** is fastest. Want me to help implement either?
